test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper sells an item for Rs. 571.20 after giving two successive discounts of 20% and 15% on its marked price. Had he not given any discount, he would have earned a profit of 12%. What is the cost price (in Rs.) of the item?
solution:
**Given:**

Selling price after two successive discounts = Rs. 571.20

First discount = 20%

Second discount = 15%

Profit without any discount = 12%

**Formula Used:**

1. Selling Price (SP) after successive discounts: SP = MP × (1 - d_1) × (1 - d_2)

2. Cost Price (CP) calculation: MP = SP / (1 + Profit Percentage)

**Calculation:**

Let the Marked Price (MP) be x .

Given two successive discounts of 20% and 15%,

Selling Price (SP) = x × (1 - 0.20) × (1 - 0.15)

⇒ 571.20 = x × 0.80 × 0.85 

⇒ 571.20 = x × 0.68

⇒ x = 571.20 / 0.68

⇒ x = 840

Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 840

Given that without any discount, the profit is 12%:

MP = CP × (1 + 12%)

⇒ 840 = CP × 1.12

⇒ CP = 840 / 1.12

⇒ CP = 750

**The cost price of the item is Rs. 750.**
